items.plain: We must stay awake to life through hope, not gadgets. People can raise their lives by deliberate effort, and the highest art is to shape the quality of each day so your whole life is worthy of your best moments.
items.core_idea: The highest art is shaping the quality of the day.

items.plain: I went to live in the woods to face only what truly matters in life, so that when I died I would not find I had never really lived.
items.core_idea: Live deliberately so you do not miss life itself.

items.plain: Our lives are wasted on endless small details. Keep things simple: reduce your concerns to a few instead of hundreds or thousands.
items.core_idea: Simplify your life; too many details fritter it away.

items.plain: Why live in such a rush and waste our lives? We worry about need before it arrives, doing a huge amount of work today to save a little tomorrow.
items.core_idea: Hurrying to prevent future trouble wastes life now.

items.plain: When we slow down and think wisely, we see that only great and worthy things truly last, and small fears and small pleasures are mere shadows. Seeing this is thrilling.
items.core_idea: Only worthy things are real; petty fears are shadows.

items.plain: A Hindu text tells of a prince raised by a forester who thought himself a commoner until told the truth. Likewise the soul mistakes its nature until a holy teacher reveals it is Brahman.
items.core_idea: The soul forgets it is divine until taught otherwise.

items.plain: People think truth lies far away in distant times and places. But every time and place is here and now; God is most fully present in this very moment and will never be more divine.
items.core_idea: Truth and God are found in the present moment.

items.plain: Let us spend one day as calmly as nature does, not knocked off course by every small disturbance. Let visitors and noise come and go while we hold steady. Why give in and simply drift with the crowd?
items.core_idea: Live one day calmly, undisturbed by small distractions.

items.plain: Whether we face life or death, we want only what is real. If we are dying, let us feel it fully; if we are alive, let us get on with living.
items.core_idea: Face reality fully, whether in dying or living.

items.plain: Time is like a shallow stream I fish in; its current slips away but eternity remains. I want to drink more deeply and fish in the sky, where the bottom is stars.
items.core_idea: Time is shallow; I long for eternity beneath it.

items.plain: When we pile up property, build families or states, or chase fame, we are mortal. But when we deal with truth we are immortal and need fear neither change nor accident.
items.core_idea: Pursuing truth makes us immortal; possessions do not.

items.plain: Somewhere there are words written for exactly our condition that could renew our lives; many have begun anew from a book. The questions troubling us troubled every wise person, and each answered them in words and life.
items.core_idea: The right book can answer the questions that trouble us.

items.plain: No method replaces staying always alert. No study, company or routine compares with really looking at what is before you. Will you merely read, or will you see? Look at what lies ahead and walk on.
items.core_idea: Seeing what is before you beats any study.

items.plain: Sometimes the present moment was too lovely to give up for work; I like a wide margin to my life. I sat whole mornings in the sun, daydreaming, and grew in those hours. They were time added, not lost.
items.core_idea: Unhurried idle hours can be growth, not waste.

items.plain: If we were always living by the best way we had learned so far, we would never be bored. Follow your own genius closely and it will show you something fresh every hour.
items.core_idea: Following your genius keeps life fresh and free of boredom.

items.plain: I admit that once I know a person's real nature, I have no hope of changing it in this life. As an Eastern saying goes, a dog's tail can be bound straight for twelve years and still curl back.
items.core_idea: A person's true nature rarely changes.

items.plain: I am glad there are owls to do the wild, mad hooting for us. Their cry suits swamps and dusky woods and speaks of a vast untamed nature, and of the dim, unsatisfied thoughts everyone has.
items.core_idea: Owls voice the dark, restless thoughts we all share.

items.plain: Feeling at one with the trembling leaves almost takes my breath away, yet like the lake my calm is rippled but not disturbed. These small waves from the evening wind are far from a storm.
items.core_idea: Calm can be rippled without being broken.

items.plain: No deep gloom can hold someone who lives close to nature with senses alive. To a healthy ear every storm is music. While I have the friendship of the seasons, I trust nothing can make life a burden.
items.core_idea: Living close to nature guards against deep gloom.

items.plain: I felt lonely only once in the woods, wondering if I needed people nearby. Then, in a gentle rain, I felt nature itself as warm, friendly company, and since then no place has seemed strange.
items.core_idea: Nature itself can be companionship in loneliness.

items.plain: What kind of distance makes a person lonely? I have found that walking closer to someone does little to bring two minds nearer together.
items.core_idea: Physical nearness does not bring minds closer.

items.plain: We let passing events shape our days, and they only distract us. Nearest to everything is the power that makes it; the grandest laws work beside us, and nearest of all is the maker whose work we are.
items.core_idea: The power that made us is nearer than any distraction.

items.plain: Confucius rightly says that goodness is never left alone like an orphan; it always draws neighbors to it.
items.core_idea: Virtue never stays alone; it attracts companions.

items.plain: By thinking, we can step back and watch events flow past like a stream. However intense my experience, part of me watches as a spectator, noting it without sharing it, as distant from me as from you.
items.core_idea: Part of us can watch our life as a spectator.

items.plain: Being alone most of the time is good for me; even the best company soon tires me. No companion is as good as solitude. We are often lonelier among people than alone; solitude is not measured in miles.
items.core_idea: Solitude is the best companion; loneliness is not distance.

items.plain: We meet too often to have anything new to offer, so we need politeness just to avoid conflict. Crowded together, we lose respect for one another; meeting less often would serve everything that truly matters.
items.core_idea: Too much company cheapens it; meet less, value more.

items.plain: Nature, in sun, wind, rain and seasons, is innocent, kind and cheering, and feels so deeply with us it would mourn anyone's just grief. Can I not commune with the earth? I am partly leaves and soil myself.
items.core_idea: We are part of a kind, sympathetic nature.

items.plain: People, like nations, need wide and natural boundaries between them, even a good stretch of neutral ground.
items.core_idea: People need generous space between them.

items.plain: In short, anyone who is alive is always at risk of dying, though the risk is smaller for someone who is half-dead already. Sitting still carries as many risks as running.
items.core_idea: Avoiding risk is its own risk; being alive is risky.

items.plain: At four I was brought through these woods to this pond, one of my oldest memories. Tonight my flute echoes over the same water. The pines still stand, and new growth rises for new young eyes.
items.core_idea: Places endure and renew across a lifetime.

items.plain: Working with your hands, even to the point of drudgery, is probably never the worst way to waste time. It always carries a lasting lesson, and for a thinker it bears fine results.
items.core_idea: Manual labor always teaches something lasting.

items.plain: I resolved that next summer I would plant virtues like sincerity, truth, simplicity, faith and innocence instead of beans, and see if they grew. Summers have passed, and I must admit to you, Reader, that those seeds never came up.
items.core_idea: Resolving to grow virtues is easier than growing them.

items.plain: Sincere people should never stand on ceremony with each other. If real worth and friendliness were there, we would not cheat, insult and shut each other out through meanness. We should not meet in such a hurry.
items.core_idea: Real friendliness drops ceremony and haste.

items.plain: It matters little whether the harvest fills the barn. The true farmer stops worrying, like squirrels that do not fret about the chestnut crop, finishes each day's work, and gives up all claim to what his fields produce.
items.core_idea: Do the work daily and let go of the outcome.

items.plain: Getting lost, even on a familiar road in a snowstorm, is valuable. We steer by habit; only when completely lost do we feel nature's vastness. Not until we have lost the world do we begin to find ourselves.
items.core_idea: Only when lost do we begin to find ourselves.

items.plain: Rulers have no need of punishment. Love goodness and the people will be good. A leader's virtue is like the wind and the people's like grass: when the wind passes over, the grass bends.
items.core_idea: Leaders who love virtue make the people virtuous.

items.plain: An old, deaf fisherman sometimes sat with me in my boat. We hardly spoke, though he hummed a psalm now and then, and our time together was perfect harmony, sweeter to remember than talk.
items.core_idea: Quiet companionship can be deeper than conversation.

items.plain: A lake is the most beautiful and expressive part of a landscape. It is the earth's eye, and looking into it, you measure the depth of your own nature.
items.core_idea: Looking into a lake, we see our own depth.

items.plain: When younger, I spent many summer mornings drifting on the pond, daydreaming; idleness was then my most fruitful work. I was rich in sunny hours, spent them freely, and do not regret missing more work.
items.core_idea: Sunny idle hours can be the richest wealth.

items.plain: Let me be poor in a way that enjoys what is truly valuable.
items.core_idea: Better to be poor and enjoy real wealth.

items.plain: Get up before dawn, free of worry, and go looking for adventure. Let midday find you at other lakes, and let night catch you anywhere, feeling at home wherever you are.
items.core_idea: Roam freely and be at home everywhere.

items.plain: Do not make earning a living your job; make it your play. Enjoy the land without owning it. People stay stuck buying and selling, living like serfs, because they lack daring and faith.
items.core_idea: Make earning a living play, not bondage.

items.plain: Most people come home each night from just next door, and their lives stagnate in the same stale air. We should come home every day from far off, from adventures, risks and discoveries, with new experience and character.
items.core_idea: Come home each day changed by new experience.

items.plain: Like most people, I find in myself both a pull toward a higher, spiritual life and a pull toward a raw, wild one, and I honor both. I love wildness as much as goodness.
items.core_idea: Honor both the spiritual and the wild in yourself.

items.plain: Lately, whenever I fish, I lose a little self-respect. I am good at it and the urge returns, but afterward I feel I should not have. It is a faint hint, but so is the first light of morning.
items.core_idea: A faint inner unease can signal a new dawn.

items.plain: Follow the faint but steady promptings of your genius, though you cannot see where they lead; no one ever followed their genius until it misled them. If you greet each day with joy, that is success.
items.core_idea: Following your genius never misleads; joy is success.

items.plain: The greatest things in life are the least noticed; we doubt and forget them, yet they are most real. The true harvest of my days is indescribable: a little stardust caught, a piece of rainbow held.
items.core_idea: Life's truest gains are intangible and easily overlooked.

items.plain: A Chinese sage says that when the soul is not its own master, we look without seeing, listen without hearing, eat without tasting. Whoever truly tastes food cannot be a glutton; whoever does not must be one.
items.core_idea: Attention to what you taste prevents gluttony.

items.plain: Our whole life is surprisingly a moral matter. Virtue and vice never stop struggling for a moment. Goodness is the only investment that never fails.
items.core_idea: Goodness is the only investment that never fails.

items.plain: We sense an animal within us that wakes as our higher nature sleeps. It is crude and sensual and may never be fully driven out; we may draw back from it, but we cannot change what it is.
items.core_idea: Our animal nature wakes when our higher nature sleeps.

items.plain: Effort brings wisdom and purity; laziness brings ignorance and sensuality. To avoid impurity and every sin, work hard, even cleaning a stable. Our nature is hard to master, but it must be mastered.
items.core_idea: Earnest work guards against laziness and impurity.

items.plain: Each person builds a temple, their body, to the god they worship, in their own style, and cannot substitute marble. We sculpt our own flesh: any nobility starts to refine our features, and any meanness or sensuality makes them brutish.
items.core_idea: How we live shapes our very body and face.

items.plain: If you just sit still long enough in a lovely spot in the woods, all its creatures will show themselves to you one by one.
items.core_idea: Sit still long enough and nature reveals itself.

items.plain: I was glad to see my work rising square and solid bit by bit, and thought that if it was going slowly, it was built to last a long time.
items.core_idea: Slow work is built to last.

items.plain: Snow had covered the ground since late November and suddenly winter surrounded me. I withdrew further into my shell and tried to keep a bright fire burning both in my house and in my heart.
items.core_idea: In winter, keep a fire burning in your heart.

items.plain: There is always a face to be seen in a fire. A worker gazing into it in the evening clears away the grime and heaviness his thoughts gathered during the day.
items.core_idea: Gazing at a fire cleanses the day's thoughts.

items.plain: Long after a house has vanished, the lilac its children planted still blooms each spring. They never imagined that small cutting would outlive them and, fifty years on, quietly tell their story to a wanderer.
items.core_idea: What we plant can outlive us and tell our story.

items.plain: There, as everywhere, I sometimes waited for the Visitor who never comes. A Hindu text says a householder should wait in his courtyard at evening for a guest. I often waited long, but no one came from town.
items.core_idea: Waiting hospitably for a visitor who never comes.

items.plain: Once a sparrow landed on my shoulder for a moment while I was hoeing, and I felt more honored by that than I would have by any military badge.
items.core_idea: Nature's small graces honor us more than rank.

items.plain: After a still winter night I woke feeling a question had been put to me. But dawn looked in calmly, asking nothing, and the snowy hill seemed to say: Forward! Nature asks no questions and answers none of ours.
items.core_idea: Nature answers our questions by simply going forward.

items.plain: Heaven is below us, right where we stand, as much as it is above us.
items.core_idea: Heaven is here on earth as well as above.

items.plain: If we knew all nature's laws, one fact would reveal everything. We know few, so our conclusions fail through our ignorance, not nature's disorder. The hidden harmony is greater still; like a mountain, truth changes with every viewpoint.
items.core_idea: Nature's harmony exceeds the few laws we know.

items.plain: A gentle thaw is more powerful than the god Thor with his hammer: the thaw melts things, while the hammer only smashes them.
items.core_idea: Gentleness melts what force can only break.

items.plain: The first sparrow of spring! The year begins with fresher hope than ever, with soft birdsong over the thawing fields. At such a moment, what do histories, traditions and written revelations matter?
items.core_idea: Spring's first birdsong outweighs all written wisdom.

items.plain: In spring the grass flames up green on the hills, a sign of endless youth; checked by frost, it keeps pushing on. So human life dies back to its root and still sends up its green blade toward eternity.
items.core_idea: Life dies to its root and grows again forever.

items.plain: The shift from storm and winter to calm, mild weather, from dark sluggish hours to bright lively ones, is a turning point that everything announces. When it finally comes, it seems to happen in an instant.
items.core_idea: The turn from winter to spring comes suddenly.

items.plain: One gentle rain greens the grass, as better thoughts brighten our outlook. We would be blessed to live always in the present, using every chance, not atoning for past neglect. We linger in winter when it is already spring.
items.core_idea: Live in the present; it is already spring.

items.plain: On a pleasant spring morning everyone's sins are forgiven; such a day is a pause from wrongdoing, and even the worst sinner may turn back. When our own innocence returns, we can see the innocence in our neighbors.
items.core_idea: Renewed innocence lets us see others' innocence.

items.plain: Village life would stagnate without the wild land around it; we need the tonic of wildness. We long to explore everything, yet need the world to stay mysterious. We can never have enough of nature's untamed vastness.
items.core_idea: We need wildness and mystery beyond our reach.

items.plain: Doctors wisely prescribe a change of scene. This place is not the whole world; wild geese and bison range far. Yet we think our fences and duties fix our fates. The universe is wider than our view of it.
items.core_idea: The universe is wider than our views of it.

items.plain: Look inward and you will find a thousand unexplored regions in your mind. Travel through them and become an expert in mapping your own inner world.
items.core_idea: Explore the undiscovered regions within your own mind.

items.plain: I left the woods for as good a reason as I went: I had other lives to live. Within a week my feet wore a path to the pond. The mind wears paths too; tradition and conformity cut deep ruts.
items.core_idea: We easily wear ruts of habit and conformity.

items.plain: My experiment taught me that if you move confidently toward your dreams and live the life you imagined, you will meet unexpected success. If you built castles in the air, they belong there; now build foundations under them.
items.core_idea: Pursue your dreams boldly, then build their foundations.

items.plain: People call moderns intellectual dwarfs beside the ancients. So what? A living dog beats a dead lion. Rather than despair at being small, be the biggest small person you can. Mind your business; be what you were made to be.
items.core_idea: Be fully what you are, not what others were.

items.plain: Why rush so desperately to succeed? If someone falls out of step, perhaps they hear a different drummer; let them step to their own music, however slow. If the life we were made for has not come, nothing substitutes.
items.core_idea: Step to the music you hear, at your own pace.

items.plain: An artist set out to make a perfect staff, since time has no part in perfect work. While he searched for wood, his friends aged and died, but he did not. He never compromised with Time, so Time spared him.
items.core_idea: Single-minded devotion to perfection is untouched by time.

items.plain: In the end nothing serves us like the truth; it alone wears well. We often live in a false position, imagining a situation and stepping into it. Say what you have to say, not what you ought; truth beats pretending.
items.core_idea: Any truth is better than make-believe.

items.plain: However poor your life is, face it and live it; do not avoid it or curse it. It is not as bad as you are. Love your life, poor as it is; sunset shines on the poorhouse as brightly too.
items.core_idea: Love your life, however poor it is.

items.plain: Grow your poverty like a garden herb. Do not chase new things, clothes or friends; return to the old. Things do not change; we do. Sell your clothes and keep your thoughts. God will see you do not lack company.
items.core_idea: Things do not change; we change.

items.plain: Even confined to an attic corner, I would find the world as large while I had my thoughts, which no one can take. Do not anxiously chase many influences; it scatters you. Humility, like darkness, reveals the heavenly lights.
items.core_idea: Humility, like darkness, reveals the heavenly lights.

items.plain: Life is sweetest lived close to the bone, and it keeps you from trifling. Being generous in higher things never costs you in lower ones. Extra wealth buys only extras; money cannot buy a single thing the soul needs.
items.core_idea: Money cannot buy anything the soul needs.

items.plain: I love to find my true bearings: not to march in showy parades, but to walk alongside the Builder of the universe if I can, and to sit thoughtfully while this restless, trivial century rushes past.
items.core_idea: Walk with the Creator while the busy age rushes by.

items.plain: Do not drive a nail into flimsy plaster; find solid wood and drive it home so well you can recall your work at night with satisfaction. Only so will God help you. Each nail is a rivet in the universe.
items.core_idea: Do every task so well you can rest easy.

items.plain: I would choose truth over love, money or fame. I once sat at a table with rich food, wine and eager servants but no sincerity or truth, and I left hungry.
items.core_idea: Without sincerity and truth, abundance leaves us hungry.

items.plain: The life within us is like a river. This year it may rise higher than ever known and flood the dry uplands; this may be the momentous year that sweeps away all our old ways.
items.core_idea: The life in us can rise beyond anything known.

items.plain: A light too bright for our eyes is darkness to us. Only the day we are awake to truly dawns. There is more day yet to come; the sun is only a morning star.
items.core_idea: Only the day we are awake to dawns.

items.plain: Should a citizen ever hand their conscience to lawmakers? Then why have one? We should be people first, subjects second. Respect for right matters more than respect for law. My only real duty is to do what I think right.
items.core_idea: Conscience and right come before obedience to law.

items.plain: Someone who gives themselves entirely to others seems useless and selfish to them, while someone who gives only partly is called a benefactor and philanthropist.
items.core_idea: Total self-giving is often misjudged; partial giving praised.

items.plain: It matters less that many people are as good as you than that there is some perfect goodness somewhere, because that will spread through and transform the whole.
items.core_idea: A little true goodness transforms the whole.

items.plain: You are not bound to devote yourself to ending even the greatest wrong; you may have other concerns. But you must not support it in practice. Before pursuing your own aims, get off the shoulders you are standing on.
items.core_idea: You need not fight every wrong, but never support it.

items.plain: How can anyone be content merely to hold an opinion that they are wronged? Cheated of a dollar, you would act. Acting on principle is revolutionary: it divides states, churches, families, even the self, separating the devilish from the divine.
items.core_idea: Acting on principle, not just opinion, changes things.

items.plain: Whatever else happens, my task is to make sure I do not lend myself to the wrong that I condemn.
items.core_idea: Never take part in the wrong you condemn.

items.plain: I was not born mainly to make the world a good place, but to live in it, good or bad. No one must do everything, only something; and being unable to do everything is no reason to do wrong.
items.core_idea: You cannot do everything, but must not do wrong.

items.plain: However small a beginning looks, whatever is done well once is done for good.
items.core_idea: What is well done is done forever.

items.plain: Is there not a kind of bloodshed when conscience is wounded? Through that wound a person's true humanity and immortality drain away until they bleed to an everlasting death.
items.core_idea: Wounding your conscience drains away your true self.

items.plain: The rich are always bound to what made them rich. The more money, the less virtue: money gets things for us and spares us hard questions. As means grow, real living shrinks. When rich, pursue your plans from poorer days.
items.core_idea: Wealth erodes virtue and narrows real living.

items.plain: When an acorn and a chestnut fall side by side, neither holds back for the other; each follows its nature and grows as best it can. A plant that cannot live by its nature dies, and so does a person.
items.core_idea: Like a plant, a person must live by their nature.

items.plain: I do not want to quarrel with anyone, person or nation. I do not want to split hairs or set myself up as better than my neighbors.
items.core_idea: No wish to quarrel or feel superior to others.

items.plain: I spend few moments actually living under a government. If a person's thought and imagination are free, and illusions do not hold them long, foolish rulers or reformers cannot seriously disrupt their life.
items.core_idea: A free mind cannot be ruled by unwise rulers.

items.plain: Those who know no purer source of truth sensibly stand by the Bible and the Constitution and drink there reverently. But those who see truth trickling in from higher up set out again on their pilgrimage toward its source.
items.core_idea: Seek truth beyond its familiar sources, toward its fountainhead.
